item.title: Why Thermodynamics Rules Future Orbital Data Centers
item.description:
📝 Indeed, the idea of data centers in orbit has gone from science fiction to a serious spending category. The Cooling Challenge in SpaceCooling is where physics separates the science from the fiction. The only cooling method available in space is radiation, and the radiator area required is derived using the Stephan-Boltzmann law.
🔗 Read more: https://spectrum.ieee.org/orbital-data-centers-heat

item.title: Driving in America Is Headlight Hell
item.description:
📝 Decades ago, the National Highway Transportation Safety Administration mandated that cars need to have separate low and high beams. Adaptive beams—which are variable in nature—don’t fit into that binary. This gets even more absurd when you consider how simple fixes have solved previous headlight woes.
🔗 Read more: https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/2026/06/car-headlights-too-bright-adaptive-beams/687488/
